description.narrative: The Project adds wastewater treatment capacity to a municipality recently exposed to surging population growth due to internally displaced people from the 2023 earthquake, and refugees from both Syria and Ukraine. The main expected project-level outcomes are from stakeholder and environmental effects by providing increased access and quality of wastewater treatment and other additional positive effects such as an integrated wastewater management system to prevent water contamination and potential waste-to-energy options. The anticipated market creation effects stem from financial integration, as IFC is offering its first blue loan to a municipality and its first blue loan in the infrastructure sector in MCT. Given the funding challenges facing most water utilities, this is expected to have demonstration and replication effects for other municipalities.

The proposed investment is an IFC A loan to Mersin Water & Sewage Administration ( MESKI), backstopped by a guarantee from Metropolitan Municipality of Mersin (MMM or City). IFC's financing will support 10 subprojects including the: (i) expansion and technology upgrade of 4 existing wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs); (ii) construction of 2 new WWTPs; and (iii) installation of 4 deep-sea discharge pipelines (collectively the Project). The Project willadd 30% (46 million cubic meters per annum) to the existing WWTP capacity in the City.
